    64→  -- velocity equations: V̇_i(t) = −(1/N) Σ_{j ≠ i} ∇W(X_i(t) − X_j(t))
    65→  (∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun t => V t i)
    66→      (-(1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, if j ≠ i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else 0)
    67→      t)

    70→-- §3  Assumption   (tex: ass:W)
    71→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    72→
    73→/-- (tex: ass:W)
    74→Standing assumption on the pair potential W : ℝ^d → ℝ.
    75→
    76→W belongs to C^{1,1}(ℝ^d): it is differentiable with a globally Lipschitz
    77→gradient.  Additionally W is even: W(−x) = W(x) for all x.
    78→The Lipschitz constant L := Lip(∇W) is finite.
    79→-/
    80→class AssW (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ) : Prop where
    81→  /-- W is continuously differentiable. -/
    82→  differentiable : Differentiable ℝ W
    83→  /-- W is even. -/
    84→  even : ∀ x : PhysSpace d, W (-x) = W x
    85→  /-- The gradient ∇W is Lipschitz with some constant L ≥ 0. -/
    86→  lipschitzGrad : ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (fun x => fderiv ℝ W x)
    87→
    88→omit [NeZero d] in
    89→/-- Helper: under `[AssW W]` (even + differentiable), the gradient of `W`
    90→at the origin vanishes.
    91→
    92→Mathematical content: differentiating `W(-x) = W(x)` at `x = 0` and using
    93→`HasFDerivAt.unique` gives `fderiv W 0 = -fderiv W 0`, hence
    94→`gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0`. In the real vector space `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`
    95→this forces `gradient W 0 = 0`.
    96→
    97→Used by `empiricalMeasureSolvesVlasov` (cor:empirical-vlasov) to kill the
    98→diagonal correction term in `weakEvolutionEmpiricalMeasure`. -/
    99→lemma gradient_zero_of_even (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ) [hW : AssW W] :
   100→    gradient W 0 = 0 := by
   101→  -- Step A: the claim that the gradient at 0 equals its own negation.
   102→  suffices h : gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0 by
   103→    -- x = -x in a ℝ-vector space ⟹ x = 0.
   104→    have h2 : gradient W 0 + gradient W 0 = 0 := by
   105→      nth_rewrite 2 [h]
   106→      exact add_neg_cancel (gradient W 0)
   107→    -- Rewrite x + x as 2 • x and use the real-vector-space cancellation.
   108→    have h3 : (2 : ℝ) • gradient W 0 = 0 := by
   109→      rw [show (2 : ℝ) • gradient W 0 = gradient W 0 + gradient W 0 from by
   110→            rw [two_smul]]
   111→      exact h2
   112→    exact (smul_eq_zero.mp h3).resolve_left (by norm_num)
   113→  -- Step B: prove gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0 via the fderiv chain rule on
   114→  -- the (trivial) composition W ∘ Neg.neg = W.
   115→  have hdiff : Differentiable ℝ W := hW.differentiable
   116→  -- Strategy: prove `gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0` by exhibiting two
   117→  -- HasFDerivAt witnesses for W at 0 and invoking uniqueness.
   118→  -- The first witness is the standard `fderiv ℝ W 0`; the second comes
   119→  -- from the chain rule on `(fun x => W (-x))`, which equals W by
   120→  -- evenness.
   121→  have h_W0 : HasFDerivAt W (fderiv ℝ W 0) 0 :=
   122→    hdiff.differentiableAt.hasFDerivAt
   123→  -- Derivative of `(fun x : PhysSpace d => -x)` at 0 is `-id` (as a CLM).
   124→  -- We get it from `hasFDerivAt_id` and `.neg` (which negates the function
   125→  -- pointwise, equivalent to applying negation to the argument).
   126→  have h_neg : HasFDerivAt (fun x : PhysSpace d => -x)
   127→      (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (PhysSpace d)) 0 :=
   128→    (hasFDerivAt_id (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : PhysSpace d)).neg
   129→  -- Need h_W0 phrased at `-(0 : PhysSpace d)` for the chain rule below.
   130→  have h_W_at_neg0 : HasFDerivAt W (fderiv ℝ W 0) (-(0 : PhysSpace d)) := by
   131→    rw [neg_zero]; exact h_W0
   132→  -- Chain rule applied to W ∘ (-·) gives `HasFDerivAt (fun x => W (-x)) ...`.
   133→  have h_chain : HasFDerivAt (fun x : PhysSpace d => W (-x))
   134→      ((fderiv ℝ W 0).comp (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (PhysSpace d))) 0 :=
   135→    h_W_at_neg0.comp 0 h_neg
   136→  -- Evenness rewrites `(fun x => W (-x))` to `W`, giving a second
   137→  -- HasFDerivAt witness for W at 0.
   138→  have hcomp_eq : (fun x : PhysSpace d => W (-x)) = W := funext hW.even
   139→  rw [hcomp_eq] at h_chain
   140→  -- Uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative.
   141→  have h_fderiv : fderiv ℝ W 0
   142→      = (fderiv ℝ W 0).comp (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (PhysSpace d)) :=
   143→    h_W0.unique h_chain
   144→  -- f.comp (-id) = -f for any CLM f.
   145→  have h_comp_neg : (fderiv ℝ W 0).comp (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (PhysSpace d))
   146→      = -(fderiv ℝ W 0) := by
   147→    ext v
   148→    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.neg_apply,
   149→               ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.map_neg]
   150→  rw [h_comp_neg] at h_fderiv
   151→  -- Push `fderiv ℝ W 0 = -fderiv ℝ W 0` through `(toDual).symm`
   152→  -- (a linear isomorphism) to land at `gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0`.
   153→  have h_grad : gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0 :=
   154→    (congrArg (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (PhysSpace d)).symm h_fderiv).trans
   155→      (map_neg _ _)
   156→  exact h_grad

   162→-- TODO(mathlib): Mathlib does not yet have a ready-made `empiricalMeasure`
   163→-- construction returning a `ProbabilityMeasure`.  We define it here as a
   164→-- placeholder using `MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac` and a finite sum.
   165→
   166→/-- (tex: def:empirical)
   167→The empirical measure of a configuration (X, V) ∈ (ℝ^d × ℝ^d)^N:
   168→
   169→  μ^N[X, V] := (1/N) Σ_{i=1}^{N} δ_{(X_i, V_i)}.

   171→Returns a `MeasureTheory.Measure (PhaseSpace d)`.  It is a probability measure
   172→when N ≥ 1.

   174→noncomputable def empiricalMeasure (N : ℕ) (X V : Fin N → PhysSpace d) :
   175→    Measure (PhaseSpace d) :=
   176→  (1 / (N : ENNReal)) • ∑ i : Fin N, Measure.dirac (X i, V i)
   177→
   178→omit [NeZero d] in
   179→/-- (tex: def:empirical)
   180→When N ≥ 1 the empirical measure is a probability measure.
   181→
   182→Proof: μ(univ) = (1/N) · Σᵢ δ_{zᵢ}(univ) = (1/N) · N · 1 = 1, where each
   183→Dirac mass evaluates to 1 on the universal set via the
   184→`Measure.dirac.isProbabilityMeasure` instance. -/
   185→lemma empiricalMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   186→    (X V : Fin N → PhysSpace d) :
   187→    IsProbabilityMeasure (empiricalMeasure N X V) := by
   188→  refine ⟨?_⟩
   189→  simp only [empiricalMeasure, Measure.smul_apply, Measure.finset_sum_apply,
   190→             measure_univ, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin,
   191→             smul_eq_mul, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   192→  exact ENNReal.div_mul_cancel
   193→    (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (NeZero.ne N)) (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top N)

   195→/-- (tex: def:empirical)
   196→The time-dependent empirical measure μ_t^N along a solution of eq:newton. -/
   197→noncomputable def empiricalMeasureCurve (N : ℕ) (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d) :
   198→    ℝ → Measure (PhaseSpace d) :=
   199→  fun t => empiricalMeasure N (X t) (V t)

   204→
   205→-- TODO(mathlib): Convolution of a function with a measure (∇W * ρ) is used
   206→-- below.  In Mathlib this would be `MeasureTheory.Measure.convolution` or a
   207→-- hand-rolled integral.  We give a local definition as a placeholder.
   208→
   209→/-- Convolution of a function k : ℝ^d → ℝ^d with a (finite) measure ρ on ℝ^d:
   210→  (k * ρ)(x) := ∫ k(x − y) dρ(y).
   211→-/
   212→noncomputable def convolveFunctionMeasure (k : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   213→    (ρ : Measure (PhysSpace d)) (x : PhysSpace d) : PhysSpace d :=
   214→  ∫ y, k (x - y) ∂ρ

   217→noncomputable def spatialMarginal (μ : Measure (PhaseSpace d)) :

   221→/-! Decomposed by sorry-decomposer.

   223→
   224→/-- The integral of a function φ against the empirical measure `empiricalMeasure N X V`
   225→equals `(1/N) * ∑ i, φ(X i, V i)`, by unfolding the weighted sum of Dirac masses. -/
   226→lemma empiricalMeasure_integral_eq (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   227→    (X V : Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   228→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ) :
   229→    ∫ z, φ z ∂(empiricalMeasure N X V) =
   230→      (1 / (N : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin N, φ (X i, V i) := by
   231→  simp only [empiricalMeasure]
   232→  rw [integral_smul_measure]
   233→  rw [integral_finset_sum_measure (fun i _ => integrable_dirac (by simp))]
   234→  simp [integral_dirac, ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_natCast, smul_eq_mul]
   235→
   236→/-- For a smooth test function φ, the chain rule gives: the map `t ↦ φ(X t i, V t i)` has
   237→derivative `⟨V t i, gradXφ (X t i, V t i)⟩ + ⟨a t i, gradVφ (X t i, V t i)⟩` at t,
   238→where `a t i` is the acceleration vector at particle i and time t.
   239→
   240→Signature refactored (Phase B of the 2026-05-25 plan): φ's Fréchet derivative is
   241→an INPUT hypothesis `hφ_fderiv` instead of being derived inside the helper.  This
   242→lifts the `ContDiff.hasFDerivAt + WithLp.toLp + gradient → toDual → toLinearMap`
   243→type-class friction up to the call site (where `ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ` is already a
   244→hypothesis and the Fréchet derivative is a one-line `have`).  The body of this
   245→helper is then a straight composition:
   246→  · `HasDerivAt.prodMk hX hV` gives the curve derivative `t ↦ (X t i, V t i)`.
   247→  · `(hφ_fderiv (X t i, V t i)).comp_hasDerivAt` composes through φ.
   248→  · Unfolding `gradXφ`/`gradVφ` via `hgradXφ`/`hgradVφ` and rewriting the
   249→    Fréchet derivative's action via `inner_product` partial-derivative
   250→    identities gives the target inner-product form. -/
   251→lemma hasDerivAt_phi_along_trajectory (N : ℕ)
   252→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   253→    (hX : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun t => X t i) (V t i) t)
   254→    (a : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   255→    (hV : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun t => V t i) (a t i) t)
   256→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ)
   257→    (φ' : PhaseSpace d → (PhaseSpace d →L[ℝ] ℝ))
   258→    (hφ_fderiv : ∀ z, HasFDerivAt φ (φ' z) z)
   259→    (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   260→    (hgradXφ : ∀ z, gradXφ z = gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1)
   261→    (hgradVφ : ∀ z, gradVφ z = gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2)
   262→    (t : ℝ) (i : Fin N) :
   263→    HasDerivAt (fun s => φ (X s i, V s i))
   264→      (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (V t i) (gradXφ (X t i, V t i)) +
   265→       @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (a t i) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))) t := by
   266→  -- Step 1: curve derivative
   267→  have hcurve : HasDerivAt (fun s => (X s i, V s i)) (V t i, a t i) t :=
   268→    (hX t i).prodMk (hV t i)
   269→  -- Step 2: compose φ through the curve
   270→  have hcomp : HasDerivAt (fun s => φ (X s i, V s i))
   271→      ((φ' (X t i, V t i)) (V t i, a t i)) t :=
   272→    (hφ_fderiv (X t i, V t i)).comp_hasDerivAt t hcurve
   273→  -- Step 3: rewrite the derivative value
   274→  convert hcomp using 1
   275→  -- Step 4: show φ'(z)(V,a) = ⟨V, gradXφ z⟩ + ⟨a, gradVφ z⟩
   276→  set z := (X t i, V t i)
   277→  -- partial x: HasFDerivAt (fun x => φ(x, z.2)) (φ' z ∘L inl ℝ _ _) z.1
   278→  have hpX : HasFDerivAt (fun x => φ (x, z.2))
   279→      ((φ' z).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inl ℝ (PhysSpace d) (PhysSpace d))) z.1 :=
   280→    (hφ_fderiv z).comp z.1 (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_left z.1 z.2)
   281→  have hpV : HasFDerivAt (fun v => φ (z.1, v))
   282→      ((φ' z).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ (PhysSpace d) (PhysSpace d))) z.2 :=
   283→    (hφ_fderiv z).comp z.2 (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_right z.1 z.2)
   284→  simp only [hgradXφ z, hgradVφ z]
   285→  -- inner(V, ∇f z.1) = fderiv f z.1 V via inner_gradient_right (real case: conj = id)
   286→  have hgX : @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (V t i) (gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1) =
   287→      fderiv ℝ (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1 (V t i) := by
   288→    rw [inner_gradient_right hpX.differentiableAt]
   289→    simp [RCLike.conj_eq_iff_re, conj_trivial]
   290→  have hgV : @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (a t i) (gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2) =
   291→      fderiv ℝ (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2 (a t i) := by
   292→    rw [inner_gradient_right hpV.differentiableAt]
   293→    simp [RCLike.conj_eq_iff_re, conj_trivial]
   294→  rw [hgX, hgV, hpX.fderiv, hpV.fderiv]
   295→  simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.inl_apply,
   296→        ContinuousLinearMap.inr_apply]
   297→  rw [← map_add]
   298→  simp [Prod.mk_add_mk]
   299→
   300→/-- The derivative of `t ↦ ∫ φ d(empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)` equals the finite sum
   301→expression `(1/N) * Σᵢ [⟨V t i, gradXφ (X t i, V t i)⟩ + ⟨aᵢ, gradVφ (X t i, V t i)⟩]`
   302→where `aᵢ = -(1/N) Σ_{j≠i} gradW(X t i - X t j)` is the Newton acceleration,
   303→obtained by combining `empiricalMeasure_integral_eq` and `hasDerivAt_phi_along_trajectory`
   304→with `HasDerivAt.sum` and `HasDerivAt.const_smul`. -/
   305→lemma hasDerivAt_empiricalIntegral_sum (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   306→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   307→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   308→    (hSol : IsNewtonSolution N gradW X V)
   309→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ)
   310→    (hφ_smooth : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ)
   311→    (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   312→    (hgradXφ : ∀ z, gradXφ z = gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1)
   313→    (hgradVφ : ∀ z, gradVφ z = gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2)
   314→    (t : ℝ) :
   315→    HasDerivAt (fun s => ∫ z, φ z ∂(empiricalMeasureCurve N X V s))
   316→      ((1 / (N : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin N,
   317→        (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (V t i) (gradXφ (X t i, V t i)) +
   318→         @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (
   319→           -(1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, if j ≠ i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else 0)
   320→           (gradVφ (X t i, V t i)))) t := by
   321→  sorry
   322→
   323→/-- Convolution of the kernel `gradW` against the spatial marginal of the
   324→empirical measure unfolds to the explicit finite sum
   325→`(1/N) • Σⱼ gradW(X t i − X t j)`.  This is the API-navigation step that
   326→separates the Measure-pushforward / Dirac-integration machinery from the
   327→algebraic "add and subtract the diagonal" step in `diagonalCorrection_eq`.
   328→
   329→Proof strategy (decomposer-supplied mathlib_hints, grep-validated against
   330→Mathlib 4.x at `.lake/packages/mathlib/`):
   331→  1. `empiricalMeasureCurve` and `empiricalMeasure` unfold to
   332→     `(1/N : ℝ≥0∞) • Σⱼ Measure.dirac (X t j, V t j)`.
   333→  2. `Measure.map_smul` (`MeasureTheory/Measure/Map.lean:127`) pushes
   334→     `Prod.fst` through the scalar.
   335→  3. `Measure.map_add` (`MeasureTheory/Measure/Map.lean:103`) + finset
   336→     induction distributes `Prod.fst` over the sum, giving
   337→     `(1/N : ℝ≥0∞) • Σⱼ Measure.dirac (X t j)`.
   338→  4. `convolveFunctionMeasure` unfolds to `∫ y, gradW(X t i − y) ∂ρ`.
   339→  5. `integral_smul_measure` (Bochner) extracts the `(1/N).toReal = 1/N`
   340→     scalar; `integral_finset_sum_measure` (`Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean:1018`)
   341→     distributes integration over the finite sum of Diracs;
   342→     `integral_dirac'` (`Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean:1131`) collapses each
   343→     summand to `gradW(X t i − X t j)`. -/
   344→lemma convolveFunctionMeasure_empiricalSpatial_eq (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   345→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   346→    (hgradW_meas : Measurable gradW)
   347→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d) (t : ℝ) (i : Fin N) :
   348→    convolveFunctionMeasure gradW
   349→        (spatialMarginal (empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)) (X t i) =
   350→      (1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, gradW (X t i - X t j) := by
   351→  -- Measurability witnesses
   352→  have hmeas_y : Measurable (fun y : PhysSpace d => gradW (X t i - y)) :=
   353→    hgradW_meas.comp (measurable_const.sub measurable_id)
   354→  have hsm_y : StronglyMeasurable (fun y : PhysSpace d => gradW (X t i - y)) :=
   355→    hmeas_y.stronglyMeasurable
   356→  have hmeas_z : Measurable (fun z : PhaseSpace d => gradW (X t i - z.1)) :=
   357→    hgradW_meas.comp (measurable_const.sub measurable_fst)
   358→  have hsm_z : StronglyMeasurable (fun z : PhaseSpace d => gradW (X t i - z.1)) :=
   359→    hmeas_z.stronglyMeasurable
   360→  -- Unfold the layered definitions.
   361→  unfold convolveFunctionMeasure spatialMarginal empiricalMeasureCurve empiricalMeasure
   362→  -- Convert integration against the pushforward (Prod.fst) to integration on the product.
   363→  rw [integral_map measurable_fst.aemeasurable hsm_y.aestronglyMeasurable]
   364→  -- Pull out the (1 / N : ℝ≥0∞) scalar.
   365→  rw [integral_smul_measure]
   366→  -- Distribute integration over the finite sum of Dirac measures.
   367→  rw [integral_finset_sum_measure (fun j _ =>
   368→        integrable_dirac' hsm_z (by simp [enorm_lt_top]))]
   369→  -- Each Dirac integral collapses to the function value at the centre.
   370→  simp only [integral_dirac' _ _ hsm_z]
   371→  -- Normalize (1/(N:ℝ≥0∞)).toReal = 1/(N:ℝ); the .1 projection collapses on pairs.
   372→  simp [ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_natCast]
   373→
   374→/-- The remainder term `r` in the weak evolution identity equals
   375→`(1/N²) * Σᵢ ⟨gradW 0, gradVφ(X t i, V t i)⟩`: this is the diagonal correction
   376→obtained when extending the Newton-equation sum `Σ_{j≠i}` to all `j` (the diagonal
   377→`j = i` summand contributes `gradW(X t i - X t i) = gradW 0`).
   378→
   379→This lemma is pure inner-product algebra atop
   380→`convolveFunctionMeasure_empiricalSpatial_eq`: extend `Σ_{j≠i}` to `Σⱼ` via
   381→`Finset.sum_ite_ne` or `Finset.sum_compl_add_sum`, distribute the inner
   382→product with `inner_sub_left`/`inner_smul_left`, recognise the
   383→`(1/N) • Σⱼ gradW` factor as the convolveFunctionMeasure unfolding. -/
   384→lemma diagonalCorrection_eq (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   385→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   386→    (hgradW_meas : Measurable gradW)
   387→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   388→    (gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   389→    (t : ℝ) :
   390→    (1 / (N : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin N,
   391→      @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (
   392→        -(1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, if j ≠ i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else 0)
   393→        (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))
   394→    = -(1 / (N : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin N,
   395→        @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _
   396→          (convolveFunctionMeasure gradW
   397→            (spatialMarginal (empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)) (X t i))
   398→          (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))
   399→      + (1 / (N : ℝ)^2) * ∑ i : Fin N,
   400→          @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (gradW 0) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i)) := by
   401→  -- Step 1: unfold the convolution form on the RHS using the proved helper.
   402→  have hconv : ∀ i : Fin N,
   403→      convolveFunctionMeasure gradW
   404→        (spatialMarginal (empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)) (X t i)
   405→      = (1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, gradW (X t i - X t j) := fun i =>
   406→    convolveFunctionMeasure_empiricalSpatial_eq N gradW hgradW_meas X V t i
   407→  -- Step 2: extend the LHS's `Σ_{j≠i}` (via the ite/0 pattern) to `Σ_j − gradW 0`.
   408→  have hext : ∀ i : Fin N,
   409→      (∑ j : Fin N, if j ≠ i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else (0 : PhysSpace d))
   410→      = (∑ j : Fin N, gradW (X t i - X t j)) - gradW 0 := by
   411→    intro i
   412→    have hsub : ∀ j : Fin N,
   413→        (if j ≠ i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else (0 : PhysSpace d))
   414→        = gradW (X t i - X t j)
   415→          - (if j = i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else (0 : PhysSpace d)) := fun j => by
   416→      by_cases hj : j = i <;> simp [hj]
   417→    simp_rw [hsub]
   418→    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_ite_eq' Finset.univ i]
   419→    simp
   420→  -- Step 3: rewrite each per-i LHS inner product into scalar form.
   421→  -- Use `real_inner_smul_left` (not generic `inner_smul_left`) to avoid a
   422→  -- `starRingEnd ℝ` wrapper on the scalar that `ring` can't see through.
   423→  have hlhs_i : ∀ i : Fin N,
   424→      @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _
   425→        (-(1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, if j ≠ i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else (0 : PhysSpace d))
   426→        (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))
   427→      = -(1 / (N : ℝ)) *
   428→          (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (∑ j : Fin N, gradW (X t i - X t j)) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))
   429→           - @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (gradW 0) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))) := by
   430→    intro i
   431→    rw [hext i, real_inner_smul_left, inner_sub_left]
   432→  -- Step 4: rewrite each per-i RHS conv-term into scalar form.
   433→  have hrhs_i : ∀ i : Fin N,
   434→      @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _
   435→        (convolveFunctionMeasure gradW
   436→          (spatialMarginal (empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)) (X t i))
   437→        (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))
   438→      = (1 / (N : ℝ)) * @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _
   439→          (∑ j : Fin N, gradW (X t i - X t j)) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i)) := by
   440→    intro i
   441→    rw [hconv i, real_inner_smul_left]
   442→  -- Step 5: substitute both rewrites and reduce to a ring identity on two abbreviated sums.
   443→  simp_rw [hlhs_i, hrhs_i]
   444→  -- Distribute the per-summand subtraction (mul_sub then sum_sub_distrib),
   445→  -- pull constants outside via reverse Finset.mul_sum, then abbreviate.
   446→  simp only [mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   447→  -- Goal is now an equation in two structural sums; ring closes the scalar identity.
   448→  ring
   449→
   450→/-- The remainder bound: for the diagonal correction `r = (1/N²) * Σᵢ ⟨gradW 0, gradVφ(zᵢ)⟩`,
   451→we have `|r| ≤ (1/N) * (⨆ x, ‖gradW x‖) * (⨆ z, ‖gradVφ z‖)`, using
   452→`abs_inner_le_norm` on each summand and the fact that the sum has N terms.
   453→
   454→The two `BddAbove` hypotheses are essential: `ciSup` over an unbounded
   455→function returns junk value 0 on `ℝ`, which would make the inequality
   456→false in the unbounded case. The .tex's `‖∇W‖_∞ ‖∇_v φ‖_∞` implicitly
   457→assumes L^∞ boundedness; making it explicit here keeps the lemma
   458→honest. (For `gradVφ`: it comes from `∇_v φ` of a smooth compactly
   459→supported `φ`, so the bound is a consequence of `HasCompactSupport`
   460→— but expressing that derivation requires Mathlib API that's awkward
   461→to assemble; easier to pass the bound as a hypothesis.) -/
   462→lemma diagonalCorrection_bound (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   463→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   464→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   465→    (gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   466→    (hgradW_bdd : BddAbove (Set.range (fun x => ‖gradW x‖)))
   467→    (hgradVφ_bdd : BddAbove (Set.range (fun z => ‖gradVφ z‖)))
   468→    (t : ℝ) :
   469→    |(1 / (N : ℝ)^2) * ∑ i : Fin N,
   470→        @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (gradW 0) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))| ≤
   471→      (1 / (N : ℝ)) * ⨆ x, ‖gradW x‖ * ⨆ z, ‖gradVφ z‖ := by
   472→  sorry
   473→
   474→/-- (tex: prop:weak)
   475→Weak evolution of the empirical measure.
   476→
   477→Let (X, V) : [0, T] → (ℝ^d × ℝ^d)^N solve the Newton equations eq:newton,
   478→and let ρ_t^N be the spatial marginal of the empirical measure μ_t^N.
   479→Then for every test function φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d × ℝ^d) and every time t,
   480→there is a real remainder r = R_N(t) such that
   481→
   482→  d/dt ⟨μ_t^N, φ⟩ = ⟨μ_t^N, v · ∇_x φ − (∇W * ρ_t^N) · ∇_v φ⟩ + r,
   483→
   484→with |r| ≤ (1/N) ‖∇W‖_∞ ‖∇_v φ‖_∞.  Concretely, r is the diagonal correction
   485→+(1/N²) Σᵢ ∇W(0) · ∇_v φ(xᵢ, vᵢ).  (The positive sign arises because extending
   486→the Newton-equation sum Σ_{j≠i} to Σ_j subtracts the j=i term `gradW(0)`,
   487→which then gets multiplied by the outer `−(1/N)` acceleration coefficient,
   488→yielding `+(1/N²)·gradW(0)·gradVφ`.)  Under Assumption ass:W (W even ⟹
   489→∇W(0) = 0) the diagonal vanishes and r = 0; that strengthening is the
   490→content of `empiricalMeasureSolvesVlasov` below.
   491→
   492→The remainder is quantified existentially because `HasDerivAt` has a
   493→unique derivative — a free `R_N` parameter would make the statement
   494→false. -/
   495→theorem weakEvolutionEmpiricalMeasure
   496→    (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   497→    (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ) [AssW W]
   498→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   499→    (hgradW : ∀ x, gradW x = gradient W x)
   500→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   501→    (hSol : IsNewtonSolution N gradW X V)
   502→    -- φ is a smooth compactly supported test function on phase space
   503→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ)
   504→    (hφ_smooth : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ)
   505→    (hφ_compact : HasCompactSupport φ)
   506→    -- ∇_x φ and ∇_v φ regarded as functions
   507→    (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   508→    (hgradXφ : ∀ z, gradXφ z = gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1)
   509→    (hgradVφ : ∀ z, gradVφ z = gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2)
   510→    -- L^∞ boundedness for ‖gradW‖ and ‖gradVφ‖, needed for the bound
   511→    -- conjunct's `ciSup` to be meaningful (without these, the sups on
   512→    -- the RHS collapse to junk value 0 on `ℝ`, making the bound vacuous
   513→    -- — and the helper `diagonalCorrection_bound` unprovable).  The
   514→    -- .tex's `‖∇W‖_∞ ‖∇_v φ‖_∞` implicitly assumes these.
   515→    (hgradW_bdd : BddAbove (Set.range (fun x => ‖gradW x‖)))
   516→    (hgradVφ_bdd : BddAbove (Set.range (fun z => ‖gradVφ z‖)))
   517→    (t : ℝ) :
   518→    -- existential witness for the remainder, with its explicit form
   519→    -- exposed so downstream corollaries (e.g. `empiricalMeasureSolvesVlasov`)
   520→    -- can compute it without re-deriving from scratch.  Concretely,
   521→    -- `r` is the diagonal correction term picked up when extending the
   522→    -- Newton-equation sum from `j ≠ i` to all `j` (the `j = i` summand
   523→    -- contributes `gradW 0`).
   524→    ∃ r : ℝ,
   525→      -- explicit formula for the remainder
   526→      r = (1 / (N : ℝ)^2) * ∑ i : Fin N,
   527→            @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (gradW 0) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i)) ∧
   528→      -- derivative identity at t
   529→      HasDerivAt (fun s => ∫ z, φ z ∂(empiricalMeasureCurve N X V s)) (
   530→        ∫ z, (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ z.2 (gradXφ z) -
   531→                @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _
   532→                  (convolveFunctionMeasure gradW
   533→                    (spatialMarginal (empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)) z.1)
   534→                  (gradVφ z))
   535→              ∂(empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)
   536→          + r) t
   537→      -- pointwise remainder bound
   538→      ∧ |r| ≤ (1 / (N : ℝ)) *
   539→          ⨆ x, ‖gradW x‖ * ⨆ z, ‖gradVφ z‖ := by
   540→  -- Provide the explicit diagonal correction as the remainder witness.
   541→  refine ⟨(1 / (N : ℝ)^2) * ∑ i : Fin N,
   542→      @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (gradW 0) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i)), rfl, ?_, ?_⟩
   543→  · -- HasDerivAt: use hasDerivAt_empiricalIntegral_sum and diagonalCorrection_eq
   544→    -- to relate the finite-sum derivative to the integral + remainder form.
   545→    have hderiv := hasDerivAt_empiricalIntegral_sum N gradW X V hSol φ
   546→      hφ_smooth gradXφ gradVφ hgradXφ hgradVφ t
   547→    -- Derive Measurable gradW from AssW W (Lipschitz fderiv ⇒ continuous gradient ⇒ measurable).
   548→    have hgradW_meas : Measurable gradW := by
   549→      have hext : gradW = fun x => gradient W x := funext hgradW
   550→      rw [hext]
   551→      obtain ⟨_, hLip⟩ := (inferInstance : AssW W).lipschitzGrad
   552→      exact ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (PhysSpace d)).symm.continuous.comp
   553→        hLip.continuous).measurable
   554→    have hcorr := diagonalCorrection_eq N gradW hgradW_meas X V gradVφ t
   555→    -- Rearrange: the derivative value from hderiv equals (integral term) + r
   556→    -- after applying hcorr to split the velocity inner products.
   557→    sorry
   558→  · -- Bound: direct application of diagonalCorrection_bound.
   559→    exact diagonalCorrection_bound N gradW X V gradVφ hgradW_bdd hgradVφ_bdd t
   560→

   562→-- §6  Equation (Weak form of empirical-measure evolution)   (tex: eq:weak-eq)
   563→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   564→
   565→/-- (tex: eq:weak-eq)
   566→The distributional evolution identity for the empirical measure (the content
   567→of Proposition prop:weak):
   568→
   569→  d/dt ⟨μ_t^N, φ⟩  =  ⟨μ_t^N, v · ∇_x φ − (∇W * ρ_t^N) · ∇_v φ⟩ + R_N(t),
   570→
   571→for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d × ℝ^d), with |R_N(t)| ≤ (1/N) ‖∇W‖_∞ ‖∇_v φ‖_∞.
   572→
   573→This is a `Prop`-valued definition packaging the statement of eq:weak-eq.
   574→-/
   575→def WeakEvolutionEq (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   576→    (μ : ℝ → Measure (PhaseSpace d))
   577→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ)
   578→    (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   579→    (R_N : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
   580→  ∀ t : ℝ,
   581→    HasDerivAt (fun s => ∫ z, φ z ∂μ s)
   582→      (∫ z, (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ z.2 (gradXφ z) -
   583→              @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _
   584→                (convolveFunctionMeasure gradW (spatialMarginal (μ t)) z.1)
   585→                (gradVφ z))
   586→        ∂μ t
   587→        + R_N t) t
   588→

   590→-- §7  Corollary (Empirical measure solves Vlasov)   (tex: cor:empirical-vlasov)
   591→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   592→
   593→/-- (tex: cor:empirical-vlasov)
   594→Under Assumption ass:W, the empirical measure μ_t^N satisfies the distributional
   595→Vlasov equation eq:vlasov with remainder R_N ≡ 0: for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d × ℝ^d),
   596→
   597→  d/dt ⟨μ_t^N, φ⟩ = ⟨μ_t^N, v · ∇_x φ − (∇W * ρ_t^N) · ∇_v φ⟩.
   598→-/
   599→theorem empiricalMeasureSolvesVlasov
   600→    (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   601→    (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ) [hW : AssW W]
   602→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   603→    (hgradW : ∀ x, gradW x = gradient W x)
   604→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   605→    (hSol : IsNewtonSolution N gradW X V)
   606→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ)
   607→    (hφ_smooth : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ)
   608→    (hφ_compact : HasCompactSupport φ)
   609→    (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   610→    (hgradXφ : ∀ z, gradXφ z = gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1)
   611→    (hgradVφ : ∀ z, gradVφ z = gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2)
   612→    -- Threaded through from `weakEvolutionEmpiricalMeasure`'s bound conjunct.
   613→    -- Not used in this corollary's body (we destructure the bound and
   614→    -- ignore it), but required by the signature of the prop:weak call.
   615→    (hgradW_bdd : BddAbove (Set.range (fun x => ‖gradW x‖)))
   616→    (hgradVφ_bdd : BddAbove (Set.range (fun z => ‖gradVφ z‖))) :
   617→    WeakEvolutionEq gradW (empiricalMeasureCurve N X V) φ gradXφ gradVφ (fun _ => 0) := by
   618→  -- WeakEvolutionEq unfolds to `∀ t, HasDerivAt ... (... + (fun _ => 0) t) t`.
   619→  intro t
   620→  -- Invoke prop:weak at this `t` and destructure the now-explicit witness.
   621→  obtain ⟨r, hr_eq, hr_deriv, _hr_bound⟩ :=
   622→    weakEvolutionEmpiricalMeasure N W gradW hgradW X V hSol φ
   623→      hφ_smooth hφ_compact gradXφ gradVφ hgradXφ hgradVφ hgradW_bdd hgradVφ_bdd t
   624→  -- Under [AssW W] we have gradW 0 = gradient W 0 = 0 (the latter via
   625→  -- the even-implies-zero-gradient helper).
   626→  have hgrad0 : gradW 0 = 0 := by
   627→    rw [hgradW]; exact gradient_zero_of_even W
   628→  -- The explicit formula for `r` collapses to 0 once gradW 0 = 0:
   629→  -- each inner product becomes ⟨0, _⟩ = 0, the finite sum is 0, and
   630→  -- the leading scalar multiplication is 0.
   631→  have hr_zero : r = 0 := by
   632→    rw [hr_eq, hgrad0]
   633→    simp [inner_zero_left]
   634→  -- Substitute r = 0 into the HasDerivAt witness; the conclusion's
   635→  -- `(fun _ => 0) t` is definitionally 0.
   636→  simpa [hr_zero] using hr_deriv
   637→

   639→-- §8  Equation (Vlasov equation)   (tex: eq:vlasov)
   640→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   641→
   642→-- TODO(mathlib): A full measure-valued notion of distributional solution to
   643→-- the nonlinear Vlasov PDE is not in Mathlib.  We define a placeholder
   644→-- predicate capturing the weak formulation.
   645→
   646→/-- (tex: eq:vlasov)
   647→The nonlinear Vlasov equation for a curve of probability measures f_t on ℝ^d × ℝ^d:
   648→
   649→  ∂_t f + v · ∇_x f − (∇W * ρ_t)(x) · ∇_v f = 0,   ρ_t(x) = ∫ f_t(x, dv).
   650→
   651→We encode this as the distributional statement: for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d × ℝ^d)
   652→the map t ↦ ∫ φ df_t satisfies
   653→
   654→  d/dt ∫ φ df_t = ∫ [v · ∇_x φ − (∇W * ρ_t)(x) · ∇_v φ] df_t.
   655→-/
   656→def IsVlasovSolution (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   657→    (f : ℝ → Measure (PhaseSpace d)) : Prop :=
   658→  ∀ (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ),
   659→    ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ → HasCompactSupport φ →
   660→    ∀ (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d),
   661→      (∀ z, gradXφ z = gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1) →
   662→      (∀ z, gradVφ z = gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2) →
   663→      WeakEvolutionEq gradW f φ gradXφ gradVφ (fun _ => 0)
   664→

   666→-- §9  Theorem (Existence and uniqueness for Vlasov)   (tex: thm:vlasov-wp)
   667→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   668→
   669→-- TODO(mathlib): `𝒫_1` (probability measures with finite first moment) is
   670→-- expressed here via `IsProbabilityMeasure` together with a `HasFiniteIntegral`
   671→-- condition on the norm.
   672→
   673→/-- Predicate: μ is a probability measure on PhaseSpace d with finite first moment. -/
   674→def HasFiniteFirstMoment (μ : Measure (PhaseSpace d)) : Prop :=
   675→  IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ Integrable (fun z : PhaseSpace d => ‖z‖) μ
   676→
   677→/-- (tex: thm:vlasov-wp)
   678→Existence and uniqueness for the Vlasov equation.
   679→
   680→Let f_0 ∈ 𝒫_1(ℝ^d × ℝ^d) be a probability measure with finite first moment.
   681→Under Assumption ass:W, there exists a unique narrowly continuous curve
   682→t ↦ f_t ∈ 𝒫_1(ℝ^d × ℝ^d) satisfying eq:vlasov in the distributional sense
   683→with f_{t=0} = f_0.
   684→-/
   685→theorem vlasovWellPosedness
   686→    (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ) [AssW W]
   687→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   688→    (hgradW : ∀ x, gradW x = gradient W x)
   689→    (f₀ : Measure (PhaseSpace d))
   690→    (hf₀ : HasFiniteFirstMoment f₀) :
   691→    ∃! f : ℝ → Measure (PhaseSpace d),
   692→      -- initial condition
   693→      f 0 = f₀ ∧
   694→      -- each f_t has finite first moment
   695→      (∀ t, HasFiniteFirstMoment (f t)) ∧
   696→      -- f solves the Vlasov equation
   697→      IsVlasovSolution gradW f ∧
   698→      -- f is narrowly continuous: t ↦ ∫ g df_t is continuous for every bounded continuous g
   699→      (∀ (g : PhaseSpace d → ℝ), Continuous g → Bornology.IsBounded (Set.range g) →
   700→        Continuous (fun t => ∫ z, g z ∂f t)) := by
   701→  sorry

   704→-- §10  Equation (Characteristic / mean-field ODE)   (tex: eq:char)
   705→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   706→
   707→-- TODO(mathlib): The self-consistent / mean-field characteristic ODE involves
   708→-- a fixed-point condition coupling the flow to the pushforward measure.
   709→-- We define the notion of a characteristic flow for a *given* curve of measures.
   710→
   711→/-- (tex: eq:char)
   712→Predicate asserting that (charX, charV) : ℝ → PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d × PhysSpace d
   713→is the characteristic flow associated to a given curve of spatial marginal measures
   714→ρ : ℝ → Measure (PhysSpace d) and pair-potential gradient gradW:
   715→
   716→  Ẋ(t, z) = V(t, z),
   717→  V̇(t, z) = −(∇W * ρ_t)(X(t, z)),
   718→  (X, V)(0, z) = z.
   719→
   720→The self-consistent condition (ρ_t is the pushforward of f_0 under X(t, ·)) is
   721→captured by `IsCharacteristicFlowSelfConsistent`.
   722→-/
   723→def IsCharacteristicFlow
   724→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   725→    (ρ : ℝ → Measure (PhysSpace d))
   726→    (charX charV : ℝ → PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d) : Prop :=
   727→  -- initial condition
   728→  (∀ z : PhaseSpace d, charX 0 z = z.1 ∧ charV 0 z = z.2) ∧
   729→  -- position ODE: Ẋ(t, z) = V(t, z)
   730→  (∀ t z, HasDerivAt (fun s => charX s z) (charV t z) t) ∧
   731→  -- velocity ODE: V̇(t, z) = −(∇W * ρ_t)(X(t, z))
   732→  (∀ t z, HasDerivAt (fun s => charV s z)
   733→      (-(convolveFunctionMeasure gradW (ρ t) (charX t z))) t)
   734→
   735→/-- (tex: eq:char)
   736→The self-consistency condition: the spatial marginal ρ_t equals the pushforward
   737→of the initial spatial marginal f₀_x under the position map X(t, ·). -/
   738→def IsCharacteristicFlowSelfConsistent
   739→    (charX : ℝ → PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   740→    (f₀ : Measure (PhaseSpace d))
   741→    (ρ : ℝ → Measure (PhysSpace d)) : Prop :=
   742→  ∀ t, ρ t = Measure.map (fun z => charX t z) f₀
   743→
   744→/-- (tex: eq:char)
   745→The Vlasov solution f_t is the pushforward of f_0 under the characteristic map
   746→(X(t,·), V(t,·)). -/
   747→noncomputable def vlasovSolutionViaPushforward
   748→    (charX charV : ℝ → PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   749→    (f₀ : Measure (PhaseSpace d)) (t : ℝ) : Measure (PhaseSpace d) :=
   750→  Measure.map (fun z => (charX t z, charV t z)) f₀
   751→

   753→-- §11  Theorem (Dobrushin, 1979)   (tex: thm:dobrushin)
   754→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   755→
   756→-- TODO(mathlib): Wasserstein-1 distance between probability measures is
   757→-- available in Mathlib as `MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.FiniteWasserstein`
   758→-- or via `MeasureTheory.Measure.HasFiniteWasserstein`, but the API is still
   759→-- developing.  We introduce a local placeholder `wasserstein1`.
   760→
   761→/-- Wasserstein-1 distance between two measures on a (pseudo)metric space,
   762→defined via the Kantorovich–Rubinstein dual formula
   763→
   764→  W₁(μ, ν) = sup { ∫ f dμ − ∫ f dν | f : 1-Lipschitz, f : α → ℝ }.
   765→
   766→Returns `ℝ≥0∞` so that unbounded suprema (e.g. when a measure has no finite
   767→first moment) are represented honestly as `⊤` rather than collapsing to the
   768→conditional-sup junk value `0` that `⨆` produces on `ℝ`.  Negative
   769→arguments to `ENNReal.ofReal` round up to `0`; that is consistent with the
   770→dual formula because the family of 1-Lipschitz `f` is closed under `f ↦ -f`,
   771→so the positive parts already realise the absolute value of the signed
   772→difference.
   773→
   774→-- TODO(mathlib): replace with Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.wasserstein`
   775→-- once the API is stable. -/
   776→noncomputable def wasserstein1 {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace α]
   777→    (μ ν : Measure α) : ENNReal :=
   778→  ⨆ (f : α → ℝ) (_ : LipschitzWith 1 f),
   779→    ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, f x ∂μ - ∫ x, f x ∂ν)
   780→
   781→/-- (tex: thm:dobrushin)
